The data dictionary: what the ids and column names in the package's data mean

Source: R/data-dictionary.R
cd_dictionary.Rd

The package names its data from a few parts: an indicator (penta1), a denominator option (anc1derived), a target population (totinftpenta) and prefixes such as cov_ (coverage) or r_ (survey estimate). This is what each part means, and how they combine. Read meanings from here, not from the spelling: anc1 and penta1 are the ANC1-derived and Penta1-derived denominators, while anc1derived and penta1derived are the population growth ones.

Usage

cd_dictionary()

Value

A list of data frames: denominators (id, label, meaning, levels, key – the label's translation key), indicators (id, label, group, computed), populations (id, label, meaning, unit), reporting_rates (id, meaning), columns (fixed column names: id, meaning) and grammar (pattern, meaning, example).

See also

cd_describe_columns() to read column names with it.

Examples

cd_dictionary()$denominators[, c("id", "label")]
#>              id                    label
#> 1            un           UN projections
#> 2         dhis2        DHIS2 projections
#> 3          anc1             ANC1-derived
#> 4        penta1           Penta1-derived
#> 5   anc1derived   ANC1 population growth
#> 6 penta1derived Penta1 population growth
